title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 'Teichmülleries' study of genus-0 moduli and real structures. To a combinatorial n-gon P_n (n points in a cyclic order) Grothendieck attaches a 'projective line' Σ = Σ_{P_n}, which contains the set S = S_{P_n} of vertices. He realises it as Σ_{\tilde P_{2n}} = P(V_{\tilde P_{2n}}). Here \tilde P_{2n} is the 'double' 2n-gon: the half-lines lying over the n points of P^1(R). V_{\tilde P_{2n}} is the real plane in which the 2n vertices sit as a centrally symmetric configuration. Concretely, V is R^2 with a regular 2n-gon, and the -1 of the vector space is the antipodal map of the 2n-gon. The dihedral group D_{\tilde P_{2n}} ≅ D_{2n} acts linearly on V. Its image in PGL(V) is D_{P_n} = D_{2n}/{±1}, acting on Σ = P^1. This gives the extension (8): 1 → {±1} → D_{2n} → D_n → 1.

This page treats n odd. (9) gives an equivalence of groupoids: pairs (2n-gon, marked sub-n-gon P'_n made of alternate vertices) ↔ n-gons, via (\tilde P_{2n}, P'_n) ↦ P'_n. For n odd, -1 swaps the two alternate sub-n-gons P'_n and P''_n. So the choice of one sub-n-gon gives a section D_{P_n} ≅ Stab(P'_n) ⊂ D_{2n}. Hence the projective action of D_{P_n} on Σ comes from a linear action on V_{\tilde P_{2n}}.

(10) identifies V_{\tilde P_{2n}} = V_{P'_n} ≅ V_{P_n}, the plane carrying a regular n-gon on which D_n acts linearly. (11) then gives Σ_{\tilde P_{2n}} = P(V_{\tilde P_{2n}}) ≅ P(V_{P_n}) = Σ_{P_n} for n odd.

He notes this identification is evident a priori. The map S_{P_n} → P(V_{P_n})(R), s ↦ Rs, is injective exactly when n is odd, since a regular n-gon then has no antipodal vertex pairs. So the n vertices give n distinct points of P^1(R) in the right cyclic order, D_n-equivariantly. The next page concludes the n-even case: Z/2n → Z/n does not split, so the D_n action on P^1 does not lift to a linear action in SL_2 (it lifts only to the binary dihedral group).

In modern terms: P^1 with n points at the n-th roots of unity is the D_n-symmetric 'centre' of a cell of M_{0,n}(R). The page is the elementary fact that dihedral subgroups D_n ⊂ PGL_2(R) lift isomorphically to GL_2(R) iff n is odd.
errors: No mathematical error. Minor notational slips: D_n is used for D_{P_n}, and D_{p_n} is written in the line about the natural operation. The equivalence (9) is stated without an explicit inverse construction, though it is clear: double the n-gon by adding antipodes.

ideas.what: Lifting the projective action of the dihedral group D_n on P^1 (n cyclically ordered points) to a linear action on a 2-dim space; the splitting of 1→±1→D_{2n}→D_n→1 holds iff n is odd, with the section given by choosing one of the two alternate sub-n-gons
ideas.modern_name: Lifting finite subgroups of PGL_2 to GL_2/SL_2; binary dihedral groups; Schur multiplier/obstruction class

ideas.what: Canonical projective line Σ_{P_n} attached to a combinatorial n-gon, realised as P(V) with vertices embedded via s ↦ Rs (injective iff n odd)
ideas.modern_name: Regular-polygon (maximally symmetric) point of a dihedral cell of M_{0,n}(R); P^1 with n-th roots of unity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; cell decomposition of M_{0,n}(R) by Kapranov, Devadoss
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the dihedral/cellular structure of M_{0,n}(R) only loosely

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but elementary bookkeeping of the classical parity phenomenon for lifting dihedral groups from PGL_2 to GL_2, in service of canonical P^1's attached to polygons. Nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'est [-aussi-] effet[?] évidente' should read 'est en effet évidente a priori'.
'Σ_{P_n} (sous P(V_{P_n}), avec un =)' is a vertical equality: Σ_{\tilde P_{2n}} written with '||' over Σ_{P_n}.
The struck line under (10) reads 'Ici Σ_{\tilde P_{2n}} s'identifie à la droite projective' (deleted); 'fournit d'ailleurs' is also partly struck.
'Dans l'opération naturelle de D_{P_n}' should read 'L'opération naturelle de D_{P_n}' (the first word is overwritten).
